current.text: He is a locked-in starter. The projected Atlanta starting five is McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Daniels, Johnson and Okongwu, and each should play 30-plus minutes.

Experts do not expect Lu Dort to take his starting job. If Dort starts, it would likely be in place of CJ McCollum. Dort and Daniels should mostly be staggered for spacing, so Dort is a small threat to his minutes.
He shot about 18% from three last season, down from 34% the season before. He shot over 30% from three over the last six weeks of the season.

Experts expect a bounce-back. His three-point percentage should rise from 18%, which would help his scoring and FG%, and his steals should not drop below two per game and could climb back toward 2.3 to 3.

Experts agree his market price is too low. Lloyd calls his rank an overreaction to him going too high last season and sees him as a round 3 to 4 player. Others say take him in the 40s or around 50. In an auction mock, 17 USD was called tremendous value, and he was expected to go over 20 USD.
Atlanta has no true point guard. McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Johnson and Daniels share the ball handling.
Quin Snyder wants Okongwu spaced away from the rim when he plays with Daniels and Johnson.
Atlanta is projected to win about 46 games and finish fourth to eighth in the East. The team was not shutting players down last season, and resting players is not a concern.
Atlanta plays 4, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21 and has 14 back-to-backs this season.

durable.text: He is an elite steals player with excellent defensive metrics. His steal totals vary from year to year.
He is not only a steals player. He grew up as a point guard, handles the ball and can give 5 to 6 assists, with good rebounds and FG% for his position.
At times he plays almost a big man role on offense.
He is a poor shooter and a poor scorer. He makes few threes and shoots a low FT% for his position.
He is worth much more in category leagues than in points leagues.

note: Daniels is a steals outlier (z +3.9) who also gives real assists, rebounds and FG%. That makes him a natural fit for punt FT% and punt 3PM builds. Yahoo values him at 17 USD and ESPN at 19 USD, but his Yahoo average cost is only 4.1 USD, and our league paid 28 USD last season. Experts see him as a round 3 to 4 value and expect him to go over 20 USD, so 18 to 24 USD is a fair range. Early in the season, check whether his three-point shooting gets back above 30%, whether his steals hold above two per game, and whether Lu Dort takes any of his minutes.
